vintage: OBR EFO October 2026, receipts Table 4.10, as policyengine-uk#2761 projects the gambling duty bases, with Machine Games Duty's 2027-28 step re-derived at the dashboard's higher-stake share
source: policyengine-uk#2761 (merged 2 November 2026), policyengine_uk/parameters/gov/economic_assumptions/yoy_growth.yaml, obr.per_capita.gambling_duty_bases: each duty's base (its receipts over the rate the model charges) per person, from HMRC's 2024-25 receipts through their 2025-26 outturn and the OBR's October 2026 Table 4.10 to 2031-32
applies_to: Every simulation built from survey data on an engine whose gambling inputs declare no uprating (policyengine-uk 2.151.0 and 2.165.1): uk_budget_data.forecast.gambling. Not a simulation built from one household's answers.
notes: Values are copied from #2761 as committed, except Machine Games Duty's 2027 value (see machine_games_higher_stake): growth per person to six decimals, by the model year (6 April) in which each fiscal year starts. The engine compounds them into an index and rounds it to five decimals; gambling.per_person_index does the same.

population_index is the ons.population index over its 2024 level that #2761 divided by (its PR body, 'Indices by year'). The national base index is the per-person index times it. The dashboard divides that by the installed engine's own ons.population growth, which grows household weights in dataset projection, so the weighted inputs grow with each duty's national base on either engine.

Machine Games Duty: a base series is Table 4.10's receipts over the rate the model charges, so it holds only if the model charges the same rate. #2761 divides the 2027-28 line by a rate that charges 90.78% of the standard-rate base at 25% (Gambling Commission Category B over Categories B and C). The dashboard's measure charges 75.7% (Category B over HMRC's whole standard-rate base), so the dashboard re-derives that one step at 75.7%: 2027 is 0.027652, not #2761's -0.003614, and the base from 2027-28 on is 3.14% above #2761's. Every other year and duty is #2761's: the rate is the same in both years of each later step, so the share cancels. machine_games_higher_stake holds the inputs, and tests/test_gambling_projection.py recomputes the value from them and #2761's value at 90.78%.
After 2031-32 the dashboard holds each base at its 2031-32 level: no policy year runs later.

machine_games_higher_stake.share_source: Gambling Commission, Industry Statistics, April 2025 to March 2026, sheet 4, K34: 2024-25 Category B gaming machine yield, £2,289.85m; over HMRC's 2024-25 standard-rate base, £604.748m of liabilities at 20% (UK Betting and Gaming Statistics, July 2026, Table_2_MGD row 20), £3,023.74m; to one decimal of a per cent. The rate the measure charges (budget_measures.machine_games_higher_stake_rate) reads it here.
machine_games_higher_stake.yield_source: Gambling Commission, Industry Statistics, April 2025 to March 2026, sheet 4, K34 and L34 (2024-25, revised), £ million, as #2761 holds them
machine_games_higher_stake.share_2761_source: policyengine-uk#2761, MACHINE_GAMES_HIGHER_STAKE_SHARE: Category B yield over Category B and C yield, 90.78%
machine_games_higher_stake.table_4_10_source: OBR EFO October 2026, detailed forecast tables, receipts Table 4.10, 'Machine games duty', 2026-27 and 2027-28, £ billion (the values #2761's tests hold)
machine_games_higher_stake.bands_source: HMRC, UK Betting and Gaming Statistics, July 2026, Table_2_MGD row 20: 2024-25 liabilities by rate over the rate (#2761's MACHINE_GAMES_BANDS)
machine_games_higher_stake.population_source: ons.population growth into 2027 in policyengine-uk 2.165.1 and #2761 (yoy_growth.yaml), which #2761 divides by
